subject: Discovery follow-up — Evaluation kickoff & next steps for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@acme-payments.com>, Alex Ramirez <alex.ramirez@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery follow-up — Evaluation kickoff & next steps for Acme Payments

Hi Claire / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the clear rundown of Acme's priorities (fraud detection at scale + lower inference cost per event). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: \

- What we heard: high-volume inference (100k+ events/day), 150ms latency target for inline scoring, strict PII controls (VPC + KMS), and desire to run a 4-week evaluation with a prompt set representative of your fraud rules.
- Redwood fit: our Dedicated pools + prefix caching can help hit latency targets and cut per-token cost; Private deployment is an option for stricter isolation.

Proposed next step: schedule an evaluation kickoff (30-45m) to align on the trial plan, success criteria, and the initial prompt/eval set. Suggested slots (PST):
- Thu Nov 5 — 10:00-10:45am
- Fri Nov 6 — 9:00-9:45am or 2:00-2:45pm

If none of these work, please propose 2 alternatives and we’ll do our best to accommodate. For the kickoff we recommend having: product/ops owner (to agree success criteria), an engineer who can provide access details for sample data, and your security contact if you want to discuss networking/KMS up front.

I attached a one-page trial plan + checklist to make the kickoff efficient (trial plan includes timeline, telemetry we’ll capture, and sample eval templates). I’ll loop Connor (solutions engineer) in the kickoff for the technical deep dive.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: Acme_Eval_TrialPlan_v1.pdf

Hi Claire — great to meet you (virtually) — thanks for scheduling. I’ll plan to cover:
- Ingestion options: S3 pull, secure streaming, or temporary S3 upload; best practice is S3 with presigned URLs for batch; streaming for live traffic tests.
- Prompt set ingestion: CSV/JSON accepted, we can walk through a small sample during the call and I’ll drop a template into the Drive link.
- Eval telemetry: latency percentiles, per-request token counts, cost estimates per 100k events.

Also to Claire / Jamal: we can start the eval on our standard evaluation agreement (no SOW required) — for Dedicated/Private you can add an order later if you decide to commit. If you’ll need a one-off NDA or PO for initial testing let us know and we’ll loop legal.

I uploaded a short checklist and a prompt ingestion template to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcmeEval (see file redwood-eval-checklist.xlsx).

Thanks — Connor
